verdict.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Coca-Cola's unit case volume growth in 2025 was driven primarily by its Latin America operating segment. This is an interpretive claim about the primary driver of growth.

Evidence E6 from the 2025 10-K shows the full-year 2025 unit case volume performance by operating segment:
- Worldwide: 0% (even)
- EMEA: 3%
- Latin America: 0% (even)
- North America: -1%
- Asia Pacific: 0% (even)

Since worldwide unit case volume was flat (0%) in 2025, and Latin America was also flat (0%), Latin America could not have been the primary driver of growth. In fact, the only segment showing positive growth was EMEA at 3%. Evidence E3 confirms that "In Latin America, unit case volume was even" for the full year 2025.

The claim is contradicted because Latin America did not drive unit case volume growth in 2025 - it was flat, while EMEA was the only segment with positive growth.

The initial verdict of CONTRADICTED is maintained after examining all challenges.

H1 (Early 2025 growth offset by later declines): REFUTED. The quarterly data shows Latin America had negative unit case volume growth in Q2 2025 (-2% for the three months ended June 27, 2025 per E11) and was even in Q3 2025 (0% for the three months ended September 26, 2025 per E10). The six-month data shows -1% and nine-month data shows -1%, indicating consistent weakness rather than early strength offset by later declines.

H2 (Rounding or different metric): REFUTED. Evidence E6 clearly shows full-year 2025 versus 2024 data with Latin America at 0% (even) for unit case volume. The quarterly tables (E10, E11) confirm this is the correct metric and time period, with consistent reporting showing Latin America at 0% for the full year.

H3 (Absolute volume contribution despite flat percentage): NO RELEVANT EVIDENCE. While E13 shows Latin America represented 13.2% of net operating revenues in 2025, there is no evidence about absolute unit case volume contributions or whether Latin America's size would make it a "primary driver" despite 0% growth. This challenge cannot be supported.

The claim states Latin America was the PRIMARY driver of unit case volume growth in 2025. The evidence clearly shows:
- Full-year 2025: Latin America 0%, EMEA +3%, North America -1%, Asia Pacific 0%, Worldwide 0%
- EMEA was the only segment with positive growth (+3%)
- Latin America was flat throughout the year

Therefore, Latin America could not have been the primary driver of growth when it had 0% growth while EMEA had 3% growth.
